scope: Non-phone native WEAPP twilight star-point display adaptation

source.interpretation: USNO defines the solar-altitude boundaries; this implementation's magnitude cutoffs are a bounded display heuristic and do not predict local naked-eye visibility.

implementation.sunFrame: skySolarLightAt selects only a valid exact report instant and rejects altitude outside [-90,90].
implementation.catalogs: BSC and SAO points share skyStarAppearance at the exact Sun altitude. Drawing and painted-object picking use the same result.
implementation.modes: Ordinary modes fade fainter stars first over 0, -6, -12 and -18 degree boundaries; warm-red Observation mode remains a lookup chart. Missing Sun data does not invent a twilight phase.
implementation.notCovered: Physical atmosphere, extinction, clouds, light pollution, horizon obstruction, deep-object overlays, planet point markers, measured visibility and target-device Canvas behavior.

desktopSimulator.fixture: MEMORY_TEST Map example spot, 2026-09-22 18:00 and 21:00 Asia/Shanghai, manual camera, 267.8 degree maximal vertical FOV
desktopSimulator.observation: The same wide-dome sunset setup formerly showed hundreds of bright stellar points. After the change, the small catalog points are absent while outlined deep-sky/chart markers, Sun and grid remain. At 21:00 the dense stellar field returns. Images were inspected visually; the old and new screenshots come from separate watch generations, so this is not a pixel-perfect controlled count.
desktopSimulator.boundary: DevTools Canvas can cover ordinary WXML controls; this observation cannot certify Android or iOS composition, touch or frame performance. No phone was used.
